It also includes 10 summaries of the model's reasoning, estimations of compute spent in terms of Pro usage on ChatGPT, and statistics about the number of attempted problems.

It is designed to handle authentication, empower consumers, and give companies visibility into what personal agents do through their websites, APIs, or company agents. Consumers decide what access to give their personal agents, and companies set parameters for what those agents can do. The protocol is open for anyone to implement.

By incorporating innovative freeform and scripted methodologies, Pantheon accumulated over a million unique tasks, overcoming traditional data limitations for enhanced AI model training.

articles.headline: OpenAI Releases Findings on 377 Math Problems, Further Roiling Field
articles.blurb: OpenAI released hundreds of new findings spanning a wide range of topics including algebra, number theory, theoretical computer science, mathematical logic, and topology. These were solved with an internal model that has not been released publicly. There is debate on whether OpenAI's systems were employing creative thinking or simply completing the final steps of a proof after borrowing ideas from human mathematicians' work. OpenAI has provided summaries of how its models came up with the solution for 10 of the problems.

articles.blurb: Apple plans to launch several devices developed through a partnership with LG as part of an ecosystem of devices that work with its new smart home hub. These include a doorbell, thermostat, an upgraded HomePod mini, and a fresh TV set-top box. The products, set to launch on October 13, will carry the LG brand. Most of the devices will include support for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Thread, and Matter.

articles.headline: Anduril's Big Week: Arsenal-2, NGC2, and a $6.6B Bet on the Future of American Shipbuilding
articles.blurb: Anduril recently announced that it was awarded a contract worth up to $1.8 billion over five years to scale Lattice across the Army's Next-Generation Command and Control effort. The company plans to build the second of its Arsenal mega-factories in Baltimore. The mega-factory will be shipbuilding-focused and will, when operations begin in 2030, span over 2 million square feet of manufacturing space. The facility will be backed by $6.6 billion across both private investment and up to $2.9 billion through a submarine production contract with the US Navy.

articles.headline: A New Trend in Nuclear Energy: Squeezing More Power Out of Old Plants
articles.blurb: Building nuclear power plants takes a long time, so some companies are looking to upgrade older reactors to squeeze even more power out of them instead. These types of upgrades can cost billions and require approval by regulators, but they can often be completed in five years or less at a fraction of the cost of building a new plant from scratch. Many tech giants are eager to pay for these upgrades to power AI. Increasing production from existing nuclear plants will add an estimated 6,000 to 8,000 megawatts of electric capacity to US grids.

articles.headline: The state of the tech industry in 2026
articles.blurb: The speed of change in the tech industry has never been this large-scale or fast. Practically nobody writes code by hand anymore. Assumptions about code output have broken, code reviews have become theatrical, and quality and reliability are down. Teams are still important, as is planning. Engineers will likely stop reading code altogether as companies start building a new type of AI infrastructure.

articles.headline: Decisions
articles.blurb: OpenAI's Decisions API turns text and images into decisions that applications can use. It evaluates text, images, or both and returns typed answers 10 times faster than the Responses API. The Decisions API returns a probability that a condition is true, a choice from a fixed set, or a score against a rubric. These answers can be used to classify content, route requests, and prioritize work in an application.

articles.headline: How to keep learning in the age of LLMs
articles.blurb: We used to learn things by doing something wrong first and then taking a lesson out of it. LLMs make everything so fast that we don't want to spend time doing the wrong things, even though it's more beneficial in the long run. The struggle is how the brain actually learns new things. Use AI to help you think through problems rather than just giving you the answer.

articles.headline: The Decision Model Gold Rush
articles.blurb: Decision models return a choice, a score, or a yes-or-no with a confidence number stapled on. Within a day of launch, TypeSafe's Jev decision model had been wired into 13% of Vercel's paid AI Gateway customer workflows, and within three days, Cloudflare, LangChain, and Langfuse had shipped integrations for it. It took competitors about two weeks to show up. The field is evolving quickly - this post looks at the criteria and nuances of using decision models in production to help readers decide which model to use.

articles.headline: Stripe agrees to acquire Parafin to expand embedded credit for small businesses
articles.blurb: Stripe has agreed to acquire embedded lending platform Parafin, which powers credit products for platforms including DoorDash, Gusto, Jobber, and Mindbody and has provided financing to more than 60,000 businesses. The deal will expand Stripe Capital with Parafin's credit, Pay Over Time, and Spend products, strengthening Stripe's push to make its 18,000+ platform customers broader financial hubs for small businesses.

articles.headline: Airwallex launches agentic business accounts for multi-entity treasury
articles.blurb: Airwallex Business Accounts now allow you to see your finances in one place and manage them with your preferred AI agent. Airwallex has rebuilt its Business Account around one view of every entity in the group, with sub-accounts for operating cash, yield, and credit. It has also added agent integration so Claude, Cursor, or any MCP client can read balances, prep FX, and issue cards inside the permissions you set.

articles.headline: EMVCo framework targets consumer intent in agentic payments
articles.blurb: EMVCo is exploring standards that would let payment participants see what a consumer authorized an AI agent to purchase, identify the agent, and flag its involvement in a transaction. The framework could give merchants, networks, and issuers important new data for fraud checks, disputes, and accountability as agents begin making card payments.

articles.headline: Robinhood Puts the Power of Hedge Funds in Every Trader's Pocket
articles.blurb: Robinhood launched Robinhood Agents, a fully embedded AI experience that can analyze the market, build strategies, and trade on your behalf around the clock, and Agent Apps, which give your Robinhood Agents another layer of intelligence with institutional-grade data and specialized tools from leading third-party providers. It also announced plans to launch 24/7 weekend trading for equities, perpetual futures for eligible US customers, earnings contracts for key company metrics, and more.

articles.headline: 🧠 Fintech is Dead
articles.blurb: Simon Taylor argues that mobile apps, cloud infrastructure, and APIs have become standard, shifting the next competitive edge to AI-driven decisions, tokenized assets, and software agents acting on customers' behalf. He points to Stripe, Ramp, and Robinhood as examples of companies building toward financial services where software handles the work and money moves around the clock.

articles.headline: Human baselines for benchmarks: AI now outperforms junior accountants
articles.blurb: A study of 12 CPAs found that frontier AI models were faster, more accurate, and dramatically cheaper than humans on four structured month-end close tasks, with Claude Opus 5 scoring 100% while accountants averaged about 37%. Mercor cautions that this does not mean accountants are broadly replaceable, since the benchmark favors detail-heavy file search and instruction following while excluding skills such as client communication, judgment, and accumulated business context, but it suggests substantial automation potential in structured accounting work.

articles.headline: London fintech enters a consolidation era as funding dries up
articles.blurb: London's fintech market is shifting from rapid startup formation toward consolidation, with funding at its lowest level since at least 2016 and capital increasingly concentrated in B2B companies and a small group of scaled winners such as Revolut, Monzo, and Wise. Consumer fintechs are losing favor, mid-stage companies face limited exit options, and many founders are responding through mergers, pivots, or acquisitions as the industry moves from unbundling financial services toward larger, rebundled platforms.

articles.headline: Amex Adds AI, Expense Tracking to Corporate Card to Counter Fintech Rivals
articles.blurb: Amex's September 30 rollout pairs a corporate cashback card with software that captures spending, generates expense reports, and flags policy violations. Aimed at businesses with $10 million to $300 million in annual revenue, it brings Amex closer to the integrated offering popularized by Ramp and Brex. Additional AI agents and accounts-payable features are planned after launch.

articles.headline: Sleepless on Wall Street: All-night stock exchanges coming soon
articles.blurb: Nasdaq, NYSE Arca, 24X National Exchange, and Cboe EDGX plan to add overnight trading from 9 PM to 4 AM ET starting December 6, pushing US equities closer to a 23/5 market and responding to growing demand from foreign investors as well as competition from crypto and prediction markets. Overnight volume is still only about 1% of total equity trading, but it has grown 358% year over year, while institutions remain cautious about thin liquidity, wider spreads, and weaker price discovery outside regular hours.

articles.headline: PayNearMe launches AI servicing and collections agent
articles.blurb: PayNearMe launched an AI agent that calls and texts customers, handles inbound inquiries, and helps customers make or schedule payments. Embedded in its PayXM platform, the agent uses payment data, business rules, and workflows to resolve issues and execute tasks, not just answer questions, with human handoffs when needed. Indiana Finance Company is piloting the tool for collections outreach and inbound support, freeing staff to focus on cases requiring personal attention.

articles.blurb: PayPal's survey suggests BNPL will play a larger role in holiday shopping this year, with 75% of consumers who have used or considered installment payments expecting to use them during the season. Consumers are still planning to spend despite higher financial anxiety, and BNPL is increasingly being used as a budgeting tool that can also lift purchase conversion for merchants.

articles.headline: ShinyHunters Extorted Boeing Spin-off Prior to Arrests
articles.blurb: A teenager from Amman, Jordan suspected of leading the prolific data theft and extortion group ShinyHunters has been detained and is reportedly cooperating with the FBI to identify other members of the hacking gang. KrebsOnSecurity has learned that the suspect, who uses the hacker handle "Rey," was detained as ShinyHunters was in the process of extorting a business unit recently divested by the global aerospace company Boeing, which manufactures the fleet of planes used by the employer of Rey's father -- Royal Jordanian Airlines.

articles.headline: Dutch Police Arrest ‘Reformed’ Hacker in Shiny Hunters Investigation
articles.blurb: Authorities in the Netherlands have arrested a 23-year-old convicted cybercriminal on suspicion of aiding in data thefts and extortions by the prolific hacker group ShinyHunters. In the days immediately following the suspect's arrest, remaining ShinyHunters members dramatically escalated their attacks, stealing highly sensitive data from the FBI and extorting the Russian ransomware group Cl0p.

articles.headline: U.S. Soldier Gets 70 Months in Prison for AT&T, Verizon Extortions
articles.blurb: A U.S. Army soldier who pleaded guilty to hacking into multiple telecommunications companies and stealing mobile call and text metadata for more than 100 million AT&T customers in 2024 was sentenced to 70 months in federal prison today and ordered to pay nearly $300,000 in restitution to victims.

articles.headline: Data Broker Radaris Loses Domains in Privacy Fight
articles.blurb: The consumer data broker Radaris.com has long had a reputation for ignoring requests to remove personal information from its vast empire of people-search services online. That reputation caught up with the company recently in a lawsuit alleging Radaris violated a New Jersey privacy law that provides for hefty fines against data brokers that publish personal information on state law enforcement officials. In the face of repeated stonewalling and prevarication by attorneys for Radaris, the judge in the case ordered that radaris.com and more than a dozen other data broker domains be transferred to the plaintiffs.

articles.headline: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
articles.blurb: Microsoft Corp. today issued updates to plug at least 974 security holes in its Windows operating systems and other software, by far its biggest single patch batch ever. Microsoft says artificial intelligence is helping to speed the discovery of vulnerabilities, but security experts warn that many organizations already are struggling to prioritize the more human-intensive endeavor of testing and deploying so many fixes each month.

articles.headline: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
articles.blurb: A new identity theft service launched on the dark web this week is selling digital scans of more than 153 million drivers licenses from people in the United States and Canada. Based on interviews with individuals whose licenses are available for purchase on this service, it appears to be siphoning images collected by a widely-used identity verification company based in Louisiana. KrebsOnSecurity also has learned that the New Orleans field office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) today launched an official inquiry into the source of the images.

articles.headline: Two Alleged ‘TeamPCP’ Hackers Arrested in Australia
articles.blurb: Authorities in Australia have arrested two men believed to be members of TeamPCP, a prolific cybercrime and data extortion group blamed for perpetrating the longest running spree of software supply chain attacks ever. In a statement released today, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) said two unnamed suspects from Western Australia, aged 21 and 23, were arrested in connection with a "sophisticated cybercrime syndicate that allegedly created malicious open-source software to rob thousands of global businesses." The AFP did not name the defendants, but KrebsOnSecurity learned the 21-year-old suspect's real identity in June, and has been communicating with him ever since. This story includes interviews with TeamPCP's self-described spokesperson, and examines clues left behind by the TeamPCP leader that likely led to his undoing.

articles.headline: Who’s Tracking You? Use This New Service to Find Out
articles.blurb: It can be daunting to determine who's responsible for showing ads on the websites we visit, or who's harvesting data from the mobile apps we use every day. That information is already semi-public, but it is not easily parsed and traditionally much of it has remained walled away in the hands of large advertising platforms. Not anymore: A powerful and free new service called DecryptAds scrapes and correlates this adtech data and makes it simple to quickly learn a great deal about the entities that are tracking you.

articles.headline: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 400 Security Holes

Connor Riley Moucka, of Kitchener, Ontario, also admitted to stealing call and text history records of more than 100 million AT&T customers.

articles.headline: No longer the same Israel? October 7th and the future of the Jewish State
articles.blurb: For now, it's still Benjamin Netanyahu’s Israel.
